prose.intro:
A standalone piece of writing: our default document type for essays, data
explainers and topic deep-dives. Published under `/{slug}`.
prose.whenToUse: - Any self-contained narrative piece that is not the entry page of a topic.
prose.whenNotToUse:
- Prefer `{template:data-insight}` for a short, chart-led observation.
- Prefer `{template:topic-page}` / `{template:linear-topic-page}` for the entry page of a topic.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The document body: a sequence of ArchieML component blocks. See the components reference for every available block.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The document type; decides the layout and where the document appears on the site.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The document headline.

fields.name: supertitle
fields.description: Kicker line shown above the title.

fields.name: subtitle
fields.description: Standfirst shown below the title.

fields.name: authors
fields.description: Comma-separated author names. Append a role in parentheses to credit a specific contribution — e.g. "Jane Doe (Editor), John Smith".

fields.name: dateline
fields.description: The publication date as displayed under the byline, e.g. "June 30, 2026".

fields.name: excerpt
fields.description: Short plain-text summary used in cards and link previews.

fields.name: refs
fields.description: Footnote definitions for ID-based references, authored as a `[.refs]` block of `id:` + `[.+content]` entries. Inline `{ref}…{/ref}` footnotes need no entry here.

fields.name: deprecation-notice
fields.description: One or more paragraphs shown in a banner marking the article as outdated, authored as a `[+deprecation-notice]` freeform block of text paragraphs.

fields.name: latest-feed-featured-image
fields.description: Image filename that overrides `featured-image` on the /latest feed.

fields.name: latest-feed-excerpt
fields.description: Rich-text excerpt (formatting and internal links allowed) shown on the /latest feed instead of `excerpt`, authored as a `[+latest-feed-excerpt]` freeform block of text paragraphs.

fields.name: hide-citation
fields.description: Set to true to hide the "Cite this work" section at the end of the article.

fields.name: cover-image
fields.description: Filename of the full-width image shown behind the header.

fields.name: featured-image
fields.description: Filename of the image used in cards and social-media previews.

fields.name: atom-title
fields.description: Title override for the document's atom-feed entry.

fields.name: atom-excerpt
fields.description: Excerpt override for the document's atom-feed entry.

fields.name: sidebar-toc
fields.description: Set to true to show a table of contents in the sidebar.

fields.name: sidebar-toc-h1-only
fields.description: Set to true to limit the sidebar table of contents to top-level headings.

fields.name: heading-variant
fields.description: Typography variant for the header: "heavy" or "light".

fields.name: hide-subscribe-banner
fields.description: Set to true to hide the subscribe banner.

fields.name: cover-color
fields.description: Named background color of the header area (one of the sdg-color-N values or "amber").

fields.name: sticky-nav
fields.description: Navigation items pinned below the header, authored as a `[.sticky-nav]` array of `target:` (anchor) + `text:` (label) pairs. Only rendered on topic pages, where it's generated automatically from heading patterns unless this array overrides it.

fields.name: details
fields.description: Details-on-demand dictionary, not authored in the document — it is merged in at render/bake time from the `dods` database table, edited at /admin/dods.

fields.name: faqs
fields.description: FAQ content consumed by data pages, authored in FAQ fragments.

skeleton.name: Opening
skeleton.description: One to three plain paragraphs stating the key message — no heading, no chart. The first paragraph doubles as what readers see in previews.

skeleton.name: Sections
skeleton.description: Each section opens with a level-1 heading and mixes prose with the evidence for it — usually a chart every few paragraphs. Callouts flag caveats or data notes; sticky-right pairs a discussion with a chart that stays on screen.

skeleton.name: Endnotes
skeleton.description: Optional closing matter — links to related work (prominent-link or recirc) and acknowledgements, often set off by a horizontal rule.

prose.intro:
The entry page for a topic: a modular page that opens with a
`{.topic-page-intro}` block and typically composes key insights, featured
metrics and an `{.all-charts}` section. Published under `/{slug}`.
prose.whenToUse: - The canonical landing page for a topic in the site navigation.
prose.whenNotToUse:
- Prefer `{template:linear-topic-page}` when the topic reads as one continuous essay.
- Prefer `{template:article}` for standalone pieces within a topic.

prose.intro:
A topic entry page that reads as one continuous essay rather than a modular
grid. Unlike `{template:topic-page}`, it gets no sticky nav — the site only renders
one for `type: topic-page`, so an authored `{guide:sticky-nav}` here has no
effect. Published under `/{slug}`.
prose.whenToUse: - A topic whose content is best presented as a single narrative flow.
prose.whenNotToUse:
- Prefer `{template:topic-page}` for modular topic pages composed of self-contained
  sections.

prose.intro:
Reusable content that is not published as a standalone page: fragments hold
shared material other documents pull in — most commonly the details-on-demand
dictionary and the FAQ content used by data pages.
prose.whenToUse:
- Content referenced from other documents or systems rather than read in
  place.
prose.notes:
## Limitations

- Most existing fragments are built around the `details` and `faqs`
  front-matter structures rather than a body — see the field descriptions
  for how each is consumed.

prose.intro:
A short, chart-led observation: a single static image or chart and a few
paragraphs making one point. Published in the data-insights feed under
`/data-insights/{slug}`.
prose.whenToUse: - One interesting pattern in the data, explained in a few hundred words.
prose.whenNotToUse:
- Prefer `{template:article}` when the piece needs sections, multiple charts, or a
  narrative arc.
prose.notes:
## Variations

- Set `grapher-url` when the insight is based on a live grapher chart,
  `narrative-chart:` when it is based on a narrative chart, and `figma-url`
  to point at the Figma file for the static image.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The insight headline.

fields.name: authors
fields.description: Comma-separated author names. Append a role in parentheses to credit a specific contribution — e.g. "Jane Doe (Editor)".

fields.name: narrative-chart
fields.description: Name of the narrative chart the insight is based on.

fields.name: grapher-url
fields.description: URL of the grapher chart the insight is based on.

fields.name: figma-url
fields.description: URL of the Figma file holding the insight's static image.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The insight body: typically one image and a handful of short text paragraphs.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Always "data-insight".

skeleton.name: The image
skeleton.description: One static chart image — the insight is the chart. The title above it states the finding, not the topic.

skeleton.name: The point
skeleton.description: Two to four short paragraphs explaining the single pattern the chart shows. Nearly every published data insight is exactly this — image plus prose, nothing else.

skeleton.name: Call to action
skeleton.description: Optional closing cta linking to the interactive chart or the related topic page.

prose.intro:
A short site-news item: a data update, website upgrade, or organizational
announcement, published in the `/latest` feed under `/latest/{slug}` and
categorized there by its kicker.
prose.whenToUse:
- Telling readers something changed on the site: refreshed data, a new
  feature, or news about the team or organization.
prose.whenNotToUse:
- Prefer `{template:data-insight}` for a chart-led observation about the data itself —
  an announcement points at what changed, it does not explain a pattern.
- Prefer `{template:article}` for any standalone narrative piece.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The announcement headline, stating the news directly — e.g. "Explore updated data on prison populations worldwide".

fields.name: excerpt
fields.description: One sentence summarizing the news, shown in the /latest feed and in link previews.

fields.name: authors
fields.description: Comma-separated author names. Append a role in parentheses to credit a specific contribution — e.g. "Jane Doe (Editor)".

fields.name: featured-image
fields.description: Filename of the image used in link previews. Published announcements rarely set one — the image in the body serves that role.

fields.name: kicker
fields.description: Short category label shown above the headline — "Data update", "Topic update", "Website upgrade", or "Announcement". Its slugified form buckets the announcement on /latest; unrecognized values are rejected at publish time.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The announcement body: a few short paragraphs, usually a closing call to action, and often one image.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Always "announcement".

skeleton.name: The news
skeleton.description: Two to five short paragraphs stating what changed and why it matters — a data update, a new feature, or organizational news. Nearly every published announcement is just prose at this length.

skeleton.name: Call to action
skeleton.description: One cta linking to the thing being announced — the updated charts, the new page, the external coverage. Almost every published announcement closes with one.

skeleton.name: The image
skeleton.description: Optional single supporting image, usually wide with an outline — most commonly a screenshot of the updated chart or feature.

prose.intro:
A profile page where an author showcases their work, generated from front
matter (name, role, bio, photo, socials) plus a body that follows one of
two layouts, chosen by how the author mostly contributes to the site.
prose.whenToUse:
- Every author with a byline on the site gets one, so their name links to
  a page collecting their work.
prose.whenNotToUse:
- Not for one-off contributors — reserve it for people with an ongoing
  publishing role.
prose.notes:
The `title` field doubles as the lookup key for "Latest work": it must
match the author's name exactly as spelled in the `authors` field of
their articles.

## Variations

Authors whose work is mostly topic pages use a single-section "topic
focus" layout instead of the two sections above: one `{.research-and-writing}`
block titled "All work", secondary links only (no primary section, no
automatic latest section, no data insights), kept up to date by hand
from `/admin/api/all-work?author=<name>`. Topic pages belong here — the
no-topics rule applies only to the article-focus "Featured work" block
above, which lists topic pills instead.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The document type; decides the layout and where the document appears on the site.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The author's name exactly as it's spelled in the `authors` field of their articles — used to filter and populate the "Latest work" section of the `{.research-and-writing}` block below.

fields.name: role
fields.description: The author's role, shown under their name.

fields.name: bio
fields.description: The author's biography, authored as a `[.+bio]` freeform block of text paragraphs.

fields.name: socials
fields.description: Links to the author's social/contact profiles, authored as a `[socials]` array of `url:` + `text:` + `type:` entries. See `{.socials}`.

fields.name: featured-image
fields.description: Filename of the author's profile picture.

fields.name: authors
fields.description: Comma-separated author names for the page's own byline (usually just the author themselves).

fields.name: body
fields.description: The page body, in one of two layouts — see the template overview above: a `{.pill-row}` of topics followed by a `{.research-and-writing}` "Featured work" block, or a single `{.research-and-writing}` "All work" block on its own.

skeleton.name: Topics
skeleton.description: A pill row listing the topics the author writes about, in a single row (about 5–7 pills max on desktop).

skeleton.name: Featured work
skeleton.description: A research-and-writing block with authors hidden on its cards, at least one primary and up to two secondary featured articles, plus an automatic "Latest work" section pulling the author's most recent articles (excluding anything already featured). No data insights or topics.

prose.intro:
A page format written once as a template and instantiated for every
country/continent in its `scope` — one published page per entity, each
with its own placeholders resolved.
prose.whenToUse:
- A topic-shaped page that should exist once per country, e.g. "CO₂ and
  Greenhouse Gas Emissions in $entityName".
prose.whenNotToUse:
- A page that doesn't vary per entity — use `{template:article}` or `{template:topic-page}`
  instead.
prose.notes:
A profile where every `{.data-callout}` fails to render for a given entity
(no data at all) is not baked for that entity; a profile where only some
callouts render is baked with the empty ones hidden. See
`{guide:profile-placeholders}`.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The document type; decides the layout and where the document appears on the site.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The document headline, with `$entityName`-style placeholders substituted per instantiated entity.

fields.name: authors
fields.description: Comma-separated author names.

fields.name: scope
fields.description: A comma-separated list that decides which entities the template is instantiated for. Each item is either `countries` (every country), `continents` (every continent), `all` (every country and continent), or the name of one specific entity, e.g. `China, North America`. Mixing the generic keywords with specific entities in the same list is allowed. A few codes work too, but only because they happen to be registered variant names, e.g. `USA`.

fields.name: exclude
fields.description: A comma-separated list of specific entity names to leave out of `scope`, e.g. `Vatican City, Christmas Island`.

fields.name: subtitle
fields.description: Standfirst shown below the title.

fields.name: excerpt
fields.description: Short plain-text summary used in cards and link previews.

fields.name: featured-image
fields.description: Filename of the image used in cards and social-media previews.

fields.name: sidebar-toc
fields.description: Set to true to show a table of contents in the sidebar.

fields.name: sidebar-toc-h1-only
fields.description: Set to true to limit the sidebar table of contents to top-level headings.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The document body: a sequence of ArchieML component blocks, usually built around `{.data-callout}` blocks that adapt to the instantiated entity. See the components reference for every available block.

fields.name: refs
fields.description: Footnote definitions for ID-based references, authored as a `[.refs]` block of `id:` + `[.+content]` entries. Inline `{ref}…{/ref}` footnotes need no entry here. See `{guide:refs}`.

skeleton.name: Opening
skeleton.description: Introductory text with entity placeholders (`$entityName`, `$EntityName`, `$noArticleEntityName`, `$entityCode`) so the copy reads naturally once instantiated for a specific country or continent.

skeleton.name: Sections
skeleton.description: Each section opens with a heading and mixes prose with data callouts that adapt to the instantiated entity — usually built around a chart per callout.

prose.intro:
The pages presenting Our World in Data itself — the organization, funding,
jobs, FAQs and policies — under the `/about` sub-navigation, whose main page
is `/about`. Published under `/{slug}`.
prose.whenToUse:
- Any page that belongs in the about-section sub-navigation rather than the
  topic content of the site.
prose.whenNotToUse:
- Prefer `{template:article}` or `{template:topic-page}` for content about the world, not about
  the organization.
prose.notes:
`{.donors}`, `{.people}`, `{.people-rows}` and `{.person}` are dedicated
about-page components, not expected to be used on other document types.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The document type; decides the layout and where the document appears on the site. Set to `type: about-page` (see `{template:about-page}`) to signify that a document belongs to the about-pages sub-navigation.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The document headline. By default about pages render with the fixed title "About" regardless of this field — see `override-title`.

fields.name: excerpt
fields.description: Short plain-text summary used in cards and link previews.

fields.name: featured-image
fields.description: Filename of the image used in cards and social-media previews.

fields.name: authors
fields.description: Comma-separated author names.

fields.name: hide-nav
fields.description: Set to true to hide the about-section sub-navigation on this page.

fields.name: override-title
fields.description: About pages render with the fixed title "About" by default, even when `title` is set (used in the gdocs index page in the admin); set this to true to use `title` on the page itself too.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The page body: a sequence of ArchieML component blocks. About pages behave like normal articles but with a few dedicated components — see `{.donors}`, `{.people}`, `{.people-rows}` and `{.person}` — that are not expected to be used outside about pages.

fields.name: refs
fields.description: Footnote definitions for ID-based references, authored as a `[.refs]` block of `id:` + `[.+content]` entries. Inline `{ref}…{/ref}` footnotes need no entry here. See `{guide:refs}`.

skeleton.name: Sections
skeleton.description: About pages behave like normal articles, built from headings, prose and images, but with dedicated spacing and typography and a shared about-section sub-navigation.

skeleton.name: Team
skeleton.description: A list of people — team members, former team members, board members — optionally wrapped in a `{.people-rows}` block to lay them out in 2 or 4 columns.

skeleton.name: Donors
skeleton.description: An empty `{.donors}` block that marks where the database-backed list of donors is inserted.

prose.intro:
The single system-managed document that renders as the site's homepage,
built from several one-off components written specifically for it.
prose.whenToUse: - Only for the one document that is the site's homepage.
prose.whenNotToUse:
- Never for authored content — most of its components (homepage search,
  homepage intro, latest data insights, key indicator collection, explorer
  tiles) are platform blocks built specifically for the homepage, not
  general-purpose building blocks for other pages.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The document type; decides the layout and where the document appears on the site. Set to `type: homepage` (see `{template:homepage}`) to mark the single document that renders as the site's homepage.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The document title. Not displayed on the homepage itself.

fields.name: authors
fields.description: Comma-separated author names.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The page body: the homepage's one-off components, in the order they should appear — see `{.pill-row}`, `{.homepage-search}`, `{.homepage-intro}`, `{.latest-data-insights}`, `{.key-indicator-collection}` and `{.explorer-tiles}`.

skeleton.name: Pill row
skeleton.description: A small grey bar of links sitting at the top of the homepage, below the nav bar.

skeleton.name: Homepage search
skeleton.description: A wide search-bar section. The nav's own search bar disappears on the homepage, so this component is required to replace it.

skeleton.name: Homepage intro
skeleton.description: A large block of links to OWID content plus hard-coded mission text — exactly 4 tiles.

skeleton.name: Latest data insights
skeleton.description: A grey section showing a scroller of the latest 7 data insights. As editorial guidance, only add the block once at least 4 are published.

skeleton.name: Key indicator collection
skeleton.description: An accordion of key indicators, each linking to a datapage.

skeleton.name: Explorer tiles
skeleton.description: A grid of links to tagged explorers.
